title: Article 58 — Qualifications for election as President

content.overview: Article 58 sets the qualifications for election as President: citizen of India; completed the age of 35 years; qualified for election as a member of the House of the People; and must not hold any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of those Governments (with specified exclusions for the President, Vice-President, Governor, and Ministers).
content.glance: Citizen + age ≥35 + qualified for LS membership + not hold office of profit (with listed exclusions).
content.study:
Article 58(1): A person is not eligible for election as President unless he—
(a) is a citizen of India;
(b) has completed the age of thirty-five years; and
(c) is qualified for election as a member of the House of the People.

Article 58(2): A person is not eligible if he holds any office of profit under the Government of India or the Government of any State or under any local or other authority subject to the control of any of the said Governments.

Explanation: the President, Vice-President, Governor, and a Minister for the Union or a State are not treated as holding an office of profit for this purpose.

Examination: citizenship; age 35; LS qualification; office-of-profit bar with constitutional exclusions.

sections.heading: Qualifications
sections.body:
1. Citizen of India.
2. Age: completed 35 years.
3. Qualified for election as a member of the Lok Sabha.
4. Must not hold office of profit (President, VP, Governor, Union/State Minister excluded from the bar).

questionsAndAnswers.question: What are the qualifications for election as President?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Under Article 58, a person must be a citizen of India, have completed the age of thirty-five years, and be qualified for election as a member of the House of the People. A person is not eligible if he holds an office of profit under the Union or a State Government or under a controlled local/other authority, but the offices of President, Vice-President, Governor, and Minister (Union or State) are not treated as offices of profit for this purpose.

examTips: Citizen; 35 years; LS qualification; office-of-profit bar with exclusions.

keyTakeaways: Art 58: citizen, 35+, LS-qualified, no office of profit (with exclusions).
